quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025) results: orders received JPY 949,683 million (+10.4%), revenue JPY 958,285 million (+10.6%), operating profit JPY 113,802 million (+16.2%; operating margin 11.9% vs 11.3%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 76,633 million (+7.3%); all record highs. Management states total orders rose because Precision Machinery orders recovered with semiconductor demand (generative AI and other uses), as some customers raised fab utilization and resumed capacity investment, while Energy orders fell from a prior year that had large projects; revenue rose in every segment. No single external customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue.

quarterly_data.signal: Precision Machinery segment FY2025: orders JPY 303,447 million (+16.7%), revenue JPY 342,267 million (+23.0%), segment profit JPY 57,773 million (+15.2%); production JPY 248,503 million (+15.5%). Management states customers' fab utilization kept recovering, led by generative-AI demand, but the full-scale resumption of capacity investment has come later than initially assumed; China's semiconductor market calmed from its earlier momentum but held a certain scale; orders and revenue rose in both products and service & support on recovering CMP and component demand. Product orders were strong for logic/foundry; memory orders exceeded the prior year, but the company expects customers' full-scale investment to resume in 2026 or later.

quarterly_data.signal: Management's view of the E-Plan2028 period for Precision Machinery (assumed market CAGR for CMP and dry pumps 8.0%): generative AI drives the market, investment for AI servers accelerates and advanced packaging technology becomes more important; US-China tension splits supply chains while new markets such as India emerge; fabs need more energy saving and responses to PFAS regulation. Segment policy: aim for the top market share in dry vacuum pumps, CMP and package plating, and establish and expand share in new equipment markets such as tape polishing equipment. For Building Service & Industrial, management expects generative AI to make data-center cooling demand surge and aims for the top position in growth markets such as data centers and electronic devices.

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 R&D expenses JPY 23,233 million, of which Precision Machinery JPY 12,009 million: improving equipment and developing new models for chip scaling, 3D integration and the increasingly important new packaging technologies demanded by fast-growing generative AI, autonomous driving and other high-performance computing; component products (as an integrated exhaust-equipment maker) with lower energy use, smaller footprint and lower environmental load; commercializing condition monitoring and predictive diagnosis; next-generation process research through joint development with customers, consortia and universities. Building Service & Industrial (R&D JPY 5,505 million) is developing industrial chillers for advanced etch equipment as etch processes move to cryogenic temperatures. Sustainability KPI: 75% progress by FY2028 in developing element technologies for 7-angstrom-generation semiconductor manufacturing.

quarterly_data.signal: Material contract: on November 12, 2025 Ebara signed a business transfer agreement with Mitsubishi Electric and a Mitsubishi Electric subsidiary to acquire, for cash through a new wholly owned subsidiary, the three-phase and IPM motor business made at Mitsubishi Electric's Nagoya Works Shinshiro plant and the industrial motor, pump and die-casting business of Mitsubishi Electric Automation (Thailand) Co., Ltd.; the transfer is scheduled during fiscal 2026. The company states the aim is to gain motor production assets, design and development capability and know-how in Japan and Thailand, accelerate global growth and offer energy-saving solutions that integrate motors with its rotation-control technology.
